boundaries: All 86 packages and 387 modules remain in scope: 46 complete packages, 199 complete modules and 228 incomplete units. Three existing related-log families receive feature-delivery annotations only. Native formatting is also exposed without inventing another algorithm family.

Native merging, interleaving, link analysis, formatting and conversion algorithms are unchanged. The fresh json_export core object adds a public delegate to the existing native log projection; no projection logic is rewritten. Other 166 core objects are reused with unchanged source/object hashes. The declaration-only header addition preserves their ABI. Server, export/formatter CLIs and six assertion-enabled suites are freshly built.

Merge and interleaving inputs are independent original File uploads with all three filenames, byte sizes and hashes in reports. They do not silently use filtered cached data. Link analysis intentionally uses the active mined session, records its source_id/counts and binds the original upload as provenance. Native source revision guards reject a stale cache before/after computation. The browser changes the backend source and verifies rejection and preceding-result retention.

All four CSV/XES input combinations retain their actual native outputs and match standalone CLI results. Duplicate relation rows expand incoming records. The controlled missing left-case relation creates an incoming case named missing; it is not silently excluded. The thirteen-row merge projects to three cases/thirteen events and opens with duplicated X/Y/Z activities intact. The larger twelve-relation merge retains forty rows.

Optional include_open_log=true serializes typed XES from the same merged EventTable through the exact existing native projection. Event/trace counts, activity attribute and completeness remain explicit. A failed projection keeps the full table and records its error; the frontend accepts valid table-only results instead of requiring a successful compatibility log. Opening remains gated on a usable, nonempty uniform activity field. Broader projection/null/type/selector fidelity remains open.

Optional include_format_table=true uses the native canonical EventTable serializer on that same result. The legacy inspection table retains its metadata schema; it cannot be passed directly to the strict formatter because it contains legacy detail fields. The canonical supplemental table avoids metadata deletion or manual reinterpretation. Native formatter success and its input_after state stay separate.

Formatting may omit rows with missing required selected fields. The UI preloads common merge selectors without running formatting automatically; users can inspect/edit them. Complete uploaded requests preserve exact bytes/options, supporting empty literal selectors and explicit nullable native options beyond blank-default form controls. Failed formatting returns actual input_after state and leaves the prior usable table available. No guarantee of a mutation for every failure is inferred.

Read-only row tables use explicit absent/null labels; typed cell inspection and raw JSON preserve their distinct native states and complete descriptors. Dtypes, index names/labels, categorical metadata, nested fields and numeric tokens remain in full JSON. Native inference/promotions, dtype/value coherence and emitted missing-value conventions remain independent parity gates; no source type conversion is reversed.

Interleavings retain native artificial boundary activities, timestamps, indices and their large time differences. The UI does not reinterpret boundary rows as ordinary source events or recompute timing differences. Native float-epoch timing precision remains a gate. Plain XES import normalizes timestamps and truncates the controlled nanosecond timestamp to microseconds: 01.123456789Z becomes 01.123456Z, changing the actual native difference. Every format-specific output remains captured verbatim rather than forced equal.

The native CSV relation adapter trims leading/trailing header whitespace, so an explicitly whitespace-padded selector failed even with a quoted header. The successful controlled custom header retains its comma/Unicode and internal-space names. Frontend query controls preserve literal selector strings; reader header/whitespace/dialect/type/ordering behavior remains an independent gate.

All eight link switch combinations match actual native/CLI outputs. Native event indices, trace/event positions, values and optional generated index fields remain in data/CSV and the graph inspector. Display limits and unit visual edge weight are geometry only; every native entry remains downloadable. Reserved generated-field collisions, extreme source sizes, ordering and broader parameter/error cases remain gates.

Full uint64 bound text reaches native unchanged. Bounds can throw explicit errors; no silent truncation or exhaustive-search guarantee is claimed. The browser verifies bound-error recovery, source-free independent uploads, active-cache link guards, forty merged rows, sixty interleavings and twenty-nine link entries with all-row exports. These are functional checks, not performance parity.

Cancellation controls/signals have unit coverage without a claim of native-computation interruption or a browser cancellation race. Active source/file changes reset results; independent workflows remain usable without a cached dataset. Returning from the global workspace preserves the existing view, and the transformation hub exposes the same controls.

Retained captures document legacy-versus-canonical metadata, XML namespaces, format-specific timestamp lexical/precision differences, trimmed CSV headers, initial graph-edge TypeScript shape and actual visible endpoint JSON versus snapshot escaping. Fresh immutable helper/output names corrected those assumptions. No reference implementation bodies or bytecode were inspected.

Final evidence binds 814 frontend tests, 589 native and 173 frontend/runtime sources, one fresh/166 reused core objects, six fresh native suites, 73 primary checks over 51 HTTP cases/18 CLI runs, 49 browser checks and 22 report/CSV/XES/table/asset checks. Eleven CSV artifacts and four native output files are independently bound. Owned server/tab are closed, viewport restored and port 8496 released; remaining catalogue workflows and full exactness/performance gates continue.
